svg.text: A harness is everything around the AI model. It turns one request into a checked, merged change, while spending as few tokens and as little time as it can. This is the pipeline as it is meant to work when every part works. The dot on each part says how far that part is today.
THE WHOLE SYSTEM IN ONE PICTURE
Every box is one pipeline. Each is drawn in full under the same letter or number. An arrow shows what one pipeline hands to another.
Reuse what a strong model worked out.

Stored so it can be trusted later.

One ordered merge at a time.
Scripts that can refuse a step.

Six stages, read left to right. Inside a stage, the steps run top to bottom.

Start with the map on the left. Every box in it is one pipeline.
Each pipeline is then drawn in full, under the same letter or number: a row of steps joined by arrows.
Inside a step: one sentence on what it does, then the parts it is made of.
The coloured line at the bottom of a step names the pipeline it feeds or uses.
Built: it exists and has run, or passed its tests.
Designed: worked out, not built yet.
Tested once, no gain yet: one form, on one repository. Not a verdict.
Token: a piece of a word. Models read, write and are metered in tokens.
Context window: everything the model reads on one call. It grows as a session goes on.
Session: one run of a model with its own context window.
Helper: a short-lived agent that a session starts for one job.
Unit: one planned job for one session.
Worktree: a separate copy of the repository on its own branch.
Hook: a script the app runs before a tool call. It can refuse the call.
Compaction: the app replaces a full window by a summary of it.
The check: the full test suite a change must pass before it lands.
Commit: one saved change in the history of the repository.
Three pipelines in a chain: the first builds a map of the code, the second learns from it, the third answers questions with it.
Turn the repository into a graph of facts. Scripts do it; no model is asked.

Today: on one repository the typed store beat scripted search by 0.076 in answer recall; three storage engines gave identical answers; a popular outside graph tool scored lower (0.564 against 0.700). Not settled: which parser builds the facts.
